summary.one_liner: Instrukt is a terminal-based AI environment for creating, instructing and sandboxing modular AI agents, with document indexes for question-answering.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a Textual-based terminal interface where users chat with and instruct AI agents using natural language. Agents are described as drop-in Python packages that can be shared, extended, and given tools. Users can build document indexes over files or code directories using Chroma and attach them to agents as a retrieval tool for question-answering. Indexing auto-detects programming languages and picks a splitting strategy for each. The README says agents can run inside Docker containers, optionally with gVisor, for isolation. It also includes an integrated prompt console with history, custom commands, an external $EDITOR option, and an IPython developer console.
use_cases: chat with a codebase using an AI assistant
building custom AI agents in Python
running AI agents in sandboxed containers
attaching tools and indexes to a terminal chatbot
how_to_run: export OPENAI_API_KEY with your OpenAI API key
If the color scheme is broken, export TERM=xterm-256color
From source: run poetry install -E all --with dev,test
notable: Agents are drop-in Python packages that can be shared and loaded by others
Automatic programming-language detection for code-aware chunking during indexing
Optional Docker sandboxing with gVisor runtime
Integrated REPL prompt with custom commands and external editor support
Built-in IPython developer console for debugging agents
caveats: README says it is a work in progress and expects bugs and API changes
Only OpenAI LLM models are currently supported; local models are a roadmap item
Supported on Linux/Mac; Windows is tested only under WSL2
